hook: "40 highly performing ad formats for your brand:" — listicle promise.
body: A numbered 40-format list (X reasons why, IG story, Us vs Them, Venn Diagram, Don't buy this, iPhone notes, ... Zero stars at #33, ... Warning at #40). No descriptions, no proof, no links — just names.
idea: "Zero stars" sits at #33 of 40 named high-performing formats — the list validates the format's existence but provides no creative detail.
sequencing: The proof gap (names only — no days-active evidence like FedotOff90's list)
formatting: Plain numbered text list; no media.
why_it_works: As a reference artifact, the bare list is skimmable and saveable — but without proof columns (unlike FedotOff90's list) it's a brainstorming seed, not validation.
what_to_steal: "Zero stars" as a named LC test: a 1-star-styled review card whose copy flips positive ("1 star because I wear it every single day and now I need more").

product: commentary — no product (a format-list post; zero stars is #10)
hook: "There are 37 ad formats printing right now." — authority list promise.
body: 10 of 37 verified formats listed with "Zero stars" at #10; longest-running example was an AI podcast at 280 days; full doc linked with live ad + days active + brand ad count per format.
cta: Doc links ("No comment or follow needed").
idea: "Zero stars" is one of 37 survival-verified money-making formats — its slot in the list is the format's proof.
why_it_works: Same as prior folders — the days-active proof column is what separates this list from bare format-name lists.
what_to_steal: Zero-stars' verified status justifies LC testing the rating-flip: empty/low stars + copy that flips the complaint into praise.
